content: Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of lorlatinib by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. It is recommended to avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of rifabutin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifabutin reduces the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of lovastatin by enhancing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapy. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of lumateperone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or efficacy of lurbinectedin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of macimorelin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers may lead to false-positive test results. Discontinue strong CYP3A4 inducers and allow for sufficient washout time before testing. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of macitentan by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of macitentan with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of maraviroc by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or effects of mestranol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to contraceptive failure. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of methadone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of methylprednisolone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of midazolam by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or effects of midostaurin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Strong CYP3A4 inducers may significantly reduce midostaurin concentrations, leading to decreased efficacy. Mifepristone increases the plasma levels or effects of rifabutin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of naldemedine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of nelfinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of rifabutin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of neratinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of neratinib with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Netupitant is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4; avoid use in patients chronically using strong CYP3A4 inducers. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of nicardipine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of nilotinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of nirogacestat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or effects of nisoldipine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable when coadministered, and there may be an increased incidence of menstruation-associated adverse effects (e.g., amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, menorrhagia). Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable when coadministered, and there may be an increased incidence of menstruation-associated adverse effects. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of norethindrone transdermal by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable when coadministered, and there may be an increased incidence of menstruation-associated adverse effects. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or effects of olaparib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of olaparib with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of olutasidenib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong or moderate CYP3A inducers decrease olutasidenib plasma concentrations and efficacy. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of omaveloxolone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of osimertinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid concomitant use of osimertinib with strong CYP3A inducers. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or effects of palbociclib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Strong CYP3A inducers decrease palbociclib plasma exposure by approximately 85%. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of palovarotene by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of pazopanib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of pemigatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or effects of perampanel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of pexidartinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Phenytoin reduces the plasma levels or effects of rifabutin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of pirtobrutinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, increase the pirtobrutinib dose to 300 mg daily (if the dose is 200 mg daily) or increase the dose by 50 mg (if the current dose is 50 mg or 100 mg daily). Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of pomalidomide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of ponatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk of ponatinib underexposure; monitor for signs of reduced efficacy. Posaconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of rifabutin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of pralsetinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. If unavoidable, double the current pralsetinib dose starting on Day 7 of coadministration with a strong CYP3A inducer. After the inducer has been discontinued for at least 14 days, resume the previous pralsetinib dose. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of praziquantel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or effects of prednisolone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of prednisone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of pretomanid by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Pretomanid is a CYP3A4 substrate; avoid coadministration of strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. Primidone decreases the plasma levels or effects of rifabutin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or efficacy of progesterone intravaginal gel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Nonhormonal contraceptives are advised. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of micronized progesterone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Nonhormonal contraceptives are advised. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of natural progesterone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Nonhormonal contraceptives are advised. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of quetiapine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or effects of quinidine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of quizartinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of ranolazine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of repaglinide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or effects of repotrectinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the plasma levels or efficacy of rifabutin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of rilpivirine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministered, increase the rilpivirine dose to 50 mg once daily; when rifabutin coadministration is stopped, decrease the rilpivirine dose to 25 mg once daily. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of rimegepant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or effects of ripretinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Coadministration with a strong CYP3A inhibitor will decrease systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite (DP-5439), potentially reducing the risk of adverse reactions. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of ritonavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of rifabutin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of rolapitant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Long-term coadministration of strong CYP3A4 inducers with rolapitant may significantly decrease its efficacy. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of romidepsin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided if possible. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or effects of selpercatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of selumetinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of silodosin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of simvastatin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or effects of siponimod by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Coadministration of siponimod with a drug that causes moderate CYP2C9 plus a moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducer is not recommended. Coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers alone is not recommended for patients with CYP2C9 1/3 and 2/3 genotypes. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of sirolimus by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of sofosbuvir by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. P-gp inducers decrease sofosbuvir levels, reducing conversion to its active metabolite (GS-331007), which is responsible for 90% of its pharmacologic effect. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Velpatasvir is a substrate of CYP2B6, CYP2C8, and CYP3A4. Drugs that are moderate-to-potent inducers of these enzymes may significantly decrease velpatasvir plasma concentrations, potentially reducing its therapeutic effect. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or effects of solifenacin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of sonidegib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of sonidegib with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. Rifabutin reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of sorafenib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Rifabutin decreases the levels or efficacy of sotorasib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
